result:
The kitchen at 3 a.m. is a different country.

I make tea I don't drink. The kettle clicks, and the apartment exhales. Outside, the streetlights bleed through curtains, making the floor look wet even though it's dry. I have been sitting here for twenty minutes trying to remember a dream I was sure mattered. It was about a train station. There were pigeons in the ceiling. A woman handed me a key made of light. I woke up when it dissolved.

Maybe that's enough.

I think a lot about how we archive ourselves. Photos, notes, half-finished emails to people we never sent them to. My phone has a folder called "ideas" with 412 voice memos. Most are me saying "okay, so..." and then silence. The rest are grocery lists. Sometimes I listen to them while walking and laugh at how serious I sounded about buying cilantro.

My neighbor practices violin at odd hours. I used to resent it. Now I find myself waiting for it, the way you wait for a bus you don't really need. It's imperfect, squeaky in the high notes, and it makes the building feel alive.

The tea is cold. I drink it anyway.

There's a kind of honesty in staying up when everyone else is asleep. No performance. No timeline. Just the hum of the refrigerator and the smell of laundry from the vent.

I should go to bed. I won't. I'll sit here longer and let the night be a room I can live in.
